title: Agent Chat: stage_screenshot is delivered to the LLM as base64 TEXT, not an image content part (vision unusable)
description:
## Verdict: BROKEN (useless base64 text, not a usable image)

When the in-app Agent Chat model calls the stage_screenshot tool, the rendered PNG reaches the model as a base64 string inside a JSON/text tool-result part, NOT as an AI SDK image/media content part. A vision model only 'sees' an image delivered as a tool-result CONTENT PART with a media part; here it just receives base64 as text it cannot decode, so the visual-inspection capability silently does nothing useful (and dumps a large text blob into context).

## Exact path (file:line)
1. Tool result shape: stage_screenshot handler returns a plain object `{ pngBase64, width, height }` — packages/authoring-ui/src/agent/registry.ts:1876-1894 (`cb.screenshotStage()` returns a base64 PNG; registry.ts:200 typedef '// returns base64 PNG'). Protocol: packages/agent-protocol/src/index.ts:623-626 + description index.ts:1084 ('Render the current stage ... to a base64 PNG').
2. Bridge delivery (the bug): packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/tools.ts:87-103 — `buildAgentTools()` defines every tool via `tool({ description, inputSchema, execute })` and `execute` just returns the plain dispatch result (tools.ts:98). There is NO `toModelOutput` / `experimental_toToolResultContent`, and NO image-content special-casing anywhere in tools.ts or agentLoop.ts (grep for image|media|toModelOutput|base64 in agentLoop.ts = zero hits).
3. AI SDK serialization: with no `toModelOutput`, AI SDK v6 (ai@6.0.208, @ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.30) serializes the returned object as a `type:'json'` ToolResultOutput (a text tool-result). The model receives the base64 as text. An image part requires `toModelOutput` returning `{ type:'content', value:[{ type:'media'|'file-data'|'image-data', data, mediaType }] }` (ToolResultOutput union, provider-utils dist/index.d.ts:749-818; toModelOutput on Tool at :1193).
4. Tool result flows into model context via streamText `response.messages` (agentLoop.ts:539-549) — confirming the base64-text tool-result becomes the next-turn ModelMessage the model reads.

## Aggravating factors
- The model is STEERED to call it: systemPrompt.ts:34 says 'To verify visual results, use stage_screenshot to render the stage to an image'. So the model will routinely call it.
- It IS in the auto-generated tool set: stage_screenshot is in ALL_COMMANDS (agent-protocol index.ts:874) so buildAgentTools exposes it.
- Context/cost harm: a full-stage PNG base64 is tens-to-hundreds of KB of TEXT per call — wasted context window + token cost, on top of being unusable.

## Vision-model dependency (note)
Even once fixed, the image part only helps if the user's chosen OpenRouter model is multimodal. OpenRouter routes per the user's model pick; a text-only model will still ignore/reject image parts. The fix should account for this.

## Fix options
1. PREFERRED: give the stage_screenshot tool a `toModelOutput` (in buildAgentTools, special-case this one command) that wraps `pngBase64` into `{ type:'content', value:[{ type:'media', mediaType:'image/png', data: pngBase64 }, optionally a text note with width/height] }` so vision models receive a real image. (`media` is deprecated-but-supported; or use `file-data`/`image-data` per provider-utils union.) Consider gating on whether the selected model is multimodal, and keeping a short text summary so text-only models still get something.
2. If client-side vision is not intended: EXCLUDE stage_screenshot from buildAgentTools (or have its execute return a short text note like 'screenshot captured, NxM' / a description) so the model doesn't waste a turn + context emitting/ingesting unusable base64. Also remove/soften the systemPrompt.ts:34 instruction.

## Scope
packages/authoring-ui/src/agentchat/tools.ts (primary); possibly systemPrompt.ts; agentchat/__tests__ for a tool-output-shape assertion. Note: the MCP server path (docs/19) already returns a proper MCP image content block per spec — this bug is specific to the in-app Agent Chat AI-SDK bridge.

## Found at
HEAD 58c4ca37b26d8889557fe8f96c19df088452b88d. Code-level confirmation (type + grep); no runtime e2e capture performed (type-level evidence is conclusive).
